Q: SwifftUI-Changing @State inside view. Should body rerender if @state property is passed to nested view? A:

Your assumption is not quite right. State does not guarantee that a view will be re-rendered or that its body will be reevaluated.

SwiftUI tracks dependencies, not ownership. A view becomes dependent on a state value when it directly reads it. Passing it down as a Binding can allow the child to update without reevaluating the parent’s body.

As for @Published, it is different because it is a Combine publisher used through ObservableObject, rather than SwiftUI-managed state.

Q: Is it possible to run a job from a running job? A:

It's a long time I'm not using SB, but I suppose you can use a JobStep as explained in official doc (https://docs.spring.io/spring-batch/reference/step/controlling-flow.html#external-flows).

If every extractionId is not mandatory to be executed with a separate job you can lookup for partinioning against `extractionId`.

If a different job is necessary for every id just inject an external service which is responsible to launch a new job using a dedicated joblauncher unbounded from default one (I suppose you can also inject the same dedicated joblauncher in your batchlet).
